transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for coming in. I need to talk to you about your imaging results from last year. I've found that we made a mistake in how we handled your follow-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? I thought everything was fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an incidental finding on your scan, something that wasn't the main reason for the test but needed to be checked again in three months. It was written in a sub-section of the report, but that part wasn't forwarded to the primary team, so we never scheduled your next appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. You're telling me you missed something? For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It has been several months since that follow-up should have happened. I am very sorry. This was our failure and I take full responsibility for the fact that this was overlooked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable! I have two kids at home. I can barely get away from my jobs to come here, and you're telling me you just forgot about me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is incredibly frustrating and it's completely unacceptable that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? I am terrified! Does this mean I have something serious? Is that why you're telling me this now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're scared, and it's completely valid to feel that way given the situation. Right now, we don't have a diagnosis, but the fact that we missed the window for that three-month check is why we need to act immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How can you just say sorry? Sorry doesn't fix the time I lost! Who even looked at my charts? Was it you? Who messed this up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it was my responsibility and the team's responsibility to ensure that every part of that report was acted upon. I failed to do that. There is no excuse for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't even believe this. I'm sitting here wondering if I'm going to be able to take care of my children and you're just telling me about a clerical error!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how overwhelming this is, especially with the pressure of working two jobs and caring for your kids. It's a heavy burden to carry on top of this news.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't even know what it's like! I don't have time for "incidental findings" and missed appointments!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that your time is limited and the stakes are high for your family. I want to make sure we fix this right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what does that even mean? What are you going to do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have already coordinated with the radiology department. I have a priority slot held for you this Friday at 9:00 AM for a repeat scan. I will personally call you on Friday afternoon by 4:00 PM to give you the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday? I have to work. I can't just leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will provide a medical note for your employers to ensure your absence is excused. Also, I've scheduled a follow-up consultation for next Tuesday at 10:00 AM so we can sit down and discuss the results in detail.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why should I trust you to do it right this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know trust is broken right now. To make sure this never happens again, I've already flagged your file with a "critical follow-up" alert and I have briefed our nursing coordinator to double-verify all imaging summaries for our patients moving forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just a nightmare. I just wanted to get better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a nightmare, and I am truly sorry that we added this stress to your life.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to go call my sister. I can't even think straight.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I have to go check on another patient now, so let's wrap this up quickly. I'll give you the appointment slips and the phone number for my direct line.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're in a hurry now? After telling me you missed my scans for months?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure you have the paperwork before I leave.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just great. Just wonderful.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be waiting for your call if you have more questions after you speak with your sister.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'll be calling. You better actually answer the phone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will. You have my direct number right here.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('let's wrap this up quickly', 'I have to go check on another patient now').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no checks for patient comprehension.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, took full responsibility without deflection, and maintained accountability throughout the patient's pushback.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('scared', 'overwhelming') and referenced the patient's specific life stressors (two jobs, children).

T.justification: The resident provided specific next steps with timelines (Friday 9am, Friday 4pm, Tuesday 10am), addressed the patient's role/needs (medical note), and explained prevention measures (critical follow-up alert).
